title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get. In insurance, paying near peak book multiples works only if the cycle and the bond curve do not compress the denominator.
epigraph.author: Institutional Underwriting Maxim

web_blocks.html: On November 20, 2026, Chubb Limited closed at $371.63 ($141.99B market cap on 382.53M shares). That price equals 13.01x trailing EPS ($28.57), 12.55x forward EPS ($29.61 implied), and 7.25x price-to-free-cash-flow [3, 32]. On balance-sheet metrics, shares trade at 1.94x reported book value per share ($191.43), 1.72x book value ex-AOCI ($216.22), and 2.47x tangible book value ex-AOCI ($150.70) [31, 33]. Shares sit above Chubb's 2016–2023 historical P/B range of 1.27x–1.65x, while Finviz consensus sits just +1.96% higher at $378.91 [30].

Cross-sector P/E screens make 12.55x forward earnings look cheap next to a 20x S&P 500. That shortcut misses two realities uncovered in our Q3 2026 audit. First, consensus models only +1.30% next-year EPS growth as commercial property softening (-5.0% YoY in Major Accounts/E&S) and +130 bps North America Commercial CAY ex-CAT combined-ratio drift (82.1%) offset 6.2% bond reinvestment yields [32, 33]. Second, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield stands at 5.04% (November 19, 2026), pushing after-tax unrealized investment losses to $(7,757)M ($(9,483)M total AOCI deficit) while 14% ($20,036M) of fixed income sits below investment grade [31, 33].

Bridging Q3's headline 84.1% combined ratio to our 86.5%–88.0% normalized cycle assumption shows why margin tailwinds are fading. Start with Q3's 82.6% consolidated CAY ex-CAT combined ratio (already ticking higher as NA Commercial CAY ex-CAT rose +130 bps YoY to 82.1%). Adding +50 to +100 bps of soft-property and social-inflation normalization yields 83.1%–83.6% underlying CAY ex-CAT. Adding +4.5 to +5.5 points for normalized catastrophes and subtracting -1.1 to -1.5 points of net favorable PPD (down from FY2025's -2.1 points as +$192M Q3 NA Commercial long-tail adverse PPD and +$224M 9M Corporate charges offset short-tail releases) bridges directly to 86.5%–88.0% [31, 32].

A Justified Price-to-Book model strips out headline multiple illusions and tests what $371.63 prices in. Using Justified P/B = (ROE - g) / (Ke - g) with a 9.75% cost of equity (reflecting the 5.04% risk-free rate, $17.53B illiquid private equity with $7.08B unfunded commitments, and long-tail casualty reserve risk) and 3.50% terminal growth, today's 1.72x ex-AOCI multiple implies a 14.25% perpetual ROE. On reported book value ($191.43), 1.94x implies a 15.63% perpetual ROE—matching Chubb's cyclical peak of 15.48% TTM ROE. Applying Bear Justified P/B (1.36x at 12.0% ROE) directly to $221E forward BVPS yields $300.56 (rounded to $301.00, -19.0% vs. CMP or -19.1% unrounded), dropping probability-weighted EV to $373.00 (+0.4% vs. CMP).

At $371.63, Base R:R is 0.42:1 and even the $355.00 50-day SMA shelf delivers just 1.18:1 EV asymmetry.

web_blocks.takeaway: Every sensitivity test lands below CMP ($323.54–$363.17), proving that paying 1.65x Base ($385.00) leaves zero safety margin for $(9,483)M AOCI, 14% below-IG bonds, $17.53B PE ($7.08B unfunded), +$192M NA Commercial adverse PPD (82.1% CAY ex-CAT CR, -5.0% property contraction), and a 10-distribution-day US Downtrend (5 CB distribution days, intraday_4h_turn: false).

web_blocks.the_number: $385.00 Base Fair Value ($373.00 probability-weighted EV, implying just +0.4% upside from $371.63 CMP and below the $378.91 Finviz consensus target).
web_blocks.how_calculated: We anchor Base Fair Value on two cross-checks: (1) 1.65x Justified P/B—from (13.8% ROE - 3.5% g) / (9.75% Ke - 3.5% g)—applied to $234E forward ex-AOCI BVPS equals $386.10; and (2) a mid-cycle 13.0x P/E on $29.61 consensus forward EPS equals $384.93. Probability-weighting 20% Bull ($430.00), 55% Base ($385.00), and 25% Bear ($301.00; 1.36x on $221E BVPS = $300.56) produces $373.00 EV.
web_blocks.the_inputs: Inputs come from Q3 2026 filings and the November 20, 2026 ledger: Q3 ex-AOCI BVPS of $216.22 ($191.43 reported), $29.61 consensus EPS (+1.30% growth), 9.75% Ke (5.04% 10Y Treasury), 3.50% g, and an 86.5%–88.0% normalized CR bridged from Q3's 82.6% consolidated / 82.1% NA Commercial CAY ex-CAT CR (+50–100 bps drift, +4.5–5.5 pts CAT load, less -1.1–1.5 pts net PPD).
web_blocks.the_range: Scenario values span $301.00 Bear ($300.56 exact: 1.36x on $221E BVPS, 10.2x Fwd EPS) to $385.00 Base (13.0x Fwd EPS) to $430.00 Bull (14.1x $30.50 EPS), compressing to $323.54–$363.17 across ROE, Ke, and AOCI stress tests.
web_blocks.if_off: If NA Commercial long-tail adverse PPD remains elevated above $192M/quarter or 10Y yields push past 5.50% (adding $3.4B+ pre-tax bond marks per 10-K Item 7A), fair value compresses toward $301–$337. Conversely, if casualty pricing beats social inflation by 300+ bps and long-tail PPD stabilizes below $150M/quarter, fair value could reach $415–$430.

web_blocks.html: Relative peer multiples on the November 20, 2026 ledger confirm why Chubb offers poor risk-reward at $371.63. Travelers (TRV) trades at $393.43 (10.3x TTM P/E, 2.78x P/B) on a 27.5% ROE, yet sits above its $382.38 Finviz consensus target. Progressive (PGR) commands 3.89x P/B for a 33.2% ROE, while Allstate (ALL) trades at 6.0x TTM P/E and 2.19x P/B on a 38.9% ROE. Reinsurer RenaissanceRe (RNR) trades at just 1.32x P/B (9.9x P/E) because TTM revenue contracted -21.2%.

Rate sensitivity and AOCI exposure explain why 1.65x forward ex-AOCI book leaves zero margin of safety. In FY2025 Form 10-K Item 7A, Chubb disclosed that a +100 bps parallel increase in interest rates reduces fixed-maturity fair value by $6.8 billion pre-tax [34]. With 5.0-year fixed-income duration (ex-Huatai), 14% below-investment-grade bonds ($20,036M), $17,528M in illiquid private equity ($7,082M unfunded commitments), and 10-year Treasuries at 5.04%, higher-for-longer yields cap reported book value ($191.43) even as reinvestment yields reach 6.2% [31, 33, 34].

Applying our anti-hedging math test settles the verdict decisively. At CMP ($371.63), Base upside to $385.00 is +$13.37 against -$31.90 downside to $339.73 (0.42:1), while probability-weighted EV ($373.00) offers just +$1.37 (+0.4%, 0.04:1). Even pulling back to the $355.00 50-day SMA shelf yields only +$18.00 EV upside against -$15.27 risk (1.18:1), failing our 1.50:1 hurdle (and even the prior $377.75 EV gave 1.49:1). Because both CMP and the 50D shelf fail 1.50:1 asymmetry while the S&P 500 sits in a 10-distribution-day Downtrend, we assign REJECTED (TIER_0).

Valuation & Trend Re-Open Trigger: Maintain REJECTED (TIER_0) above $345.00 because CMP ($371.63; 0.42:1 Base / +0.4% EV) and the $355.00 50D shelf (1.18:1 EV R:R) fail our 1.50:1 gate. Re-open underwriting review strictly below $330.00–$345.00 ONLY if S&P 500 exits Downtrend, 4H/daily trend turns upward, and NA Commercial long-tail adverse PPD stabilizes below $150M–$192M/quarter.

book_paragraphs: After six chapters inside Chubb's underwriting engine without looking at a stock quote, it is time to open the November 20, 2026 market ledger. Chubb closed at $371.63, giving the company a $141.99 billion market value. That price equates to 13.01 times trailing earnings of $28.57 per share, 12.55 times forward earnings, 1.94 times reported book value of $191.43, and 1.72 times ex-AOCI book value of $216.22.

At first glance, 12.55 times forward earnings looks like a bargain in a U.S. market near 20 times earnings. Do not fall for that cross-sector shortcut. Wall Street consensus projects next-year EPS growth of just 1.30%, and the average analyst target sits at $378.91—barely 2% above the current share price. Why is growth flattening? Because large-account commercial property rates are softening (-5.0% YoY in Major Accounts/E&S), North America Commercial CAY ex-CAT combined ratio drifted +130 bps higher to 82.1%, and our quantitative bridge puts normalized consolidated combined ratio at 86.5%–88.0% rather than Q3's 84.1%.

Meanwhile, our Pass 1 footnote audit uncovered balance-sheet details that forbid paying peak book multiples. With 10-year U.S. Treasury yields at 5.04%, Chubb's AOCI deficit reached negative $9.48 billion (negative $7.76 billion in after-tax unrealized bond losses). Fourteen percent of the fixed-income book—$20.04 billion—sits below investment grade, alongside $17.53 billion in illiquid private equity funds with $7.08 billion in unfunded commitments, plus $192 million in third-quarter adverse long-tail casualty development in North America Commercial.

When we run our Justified Price-to-Book model with a 9.75% cost of equity and 3.50% terminal growth, Base Fair Value sits at $385.00 (1.65x on $234E forward ex-AOCI BVPS), while Bull sits at $430.00. Crucially, reconciling the Bear Case strictly to its 1.36x Justified P/B (at 12.0% ROE) on $221E BVPS produces $300.56—rounded to $301.00 (-19.0% vs. CMP, or -19.1% unrounded). That pulls our probability-weighted Expected Value down to $373.00, just +0.4% above today's $371.63 close.

That honest valuation check forces a decisive rejection rather than a timid hedge. Against the $339.73 snapshot stop reference, CMP offers just 0.42-to-1 Base asymmetry and 0.04-to-1 EV asymmetry. Even a pullback to the $355.00 50-day moving average yields only 1.18-to-1 asymmetry on our $373.00 Expected Value—failing our 1.50-to-1 portfolio hurdle. Rather than stretching targets or hiding behind WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT, we assign REJECTED (TIER_0) and wait for a deeper $330.00–$345.00 valuation and trend reset.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: ZERO SAFETY MARGIN MEANS REJECT, NOT HEDGE
book_callouts.text: When Bear Justified P/B (1.36x on $221E BV) lands at $301.00 and probability-weighted EV drops to $373.00, even a 50-day SMA pullback to $355.00 yields just 1.18:1 asymmetry. Refuse to use WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT as an escape hatch—assign REJECTED (TIER_0) and protect cash.

book_subsections.title: Bridging Q3's 84.1% Combined Ratio to 86.5%–88.0% Normalized Economics
paragraphs: Retail screens see an 84.1% Q3 combined ratio and assume Chubb can earn 15%-plus ROE indefinitely. Look under the hood using our quantitative bridge. Start with Q3's 82.6% consolidated current-accident-year ex-CAT combined ratio, where North America Commercial already ticked up 130 basis points year-over-year to 82.1% as Major Accounts property contracted 5.0%.

Add 50 to 100 basis points for ongoing property rate softening and social-inflation drift (reaching 83.1%–83.6%), add 4.5 to 5.5 points of normalized annual catastrophe losses, and subtract 1.1 to 1.5 points of normalized favorable reserve releases (compressed by +$192 million in Q3 NA Commercial long-tail adverse PPD and +$224 million in 9M Corporate run-off). The sum lands cleanly at an 86.5%–88.0% normalized combined ratio.

book_subsections.title: Sensitivity Stress Tests: Why $385.00 Leaves Zero Margin for Error
paragraphs: Our four-row sensitivity table exposes how fragile the valuation is at $371.63. If normalized ROE compresses modestly to 12.5%–13.2%, Justified P/B drops to 1.44x–1.55x ($336.96–$363.17). If 14% below-IG bonds, $17.53 billion of illiquid private equity, and a 10-distribution-day US Downtrend add +100 bps to cost of equity (10.75% Ke), fair value drops to $332.44.

If half of today's $24.79-per-share AOCI deficit persists alongside a 1.46x multiple de-rating, fair value falls to $323.54—and full Bear (1.36x on $221E BVPS) sits at $300.56 ($301.00). Comparing Chubb against peers on the November 20 ledger—Travelers at 10.3x P/E (2.78x P/B), Progressive at 3.89x P/B, Allstate at 6.0x TTM P/E (2.19x P/B), and RenaissanceRe at 1.32x P/B—confirms that Chubb offers zero margin of safety above $345.00.

book_subsections.title: Why Every Valuation Stress Test Points Below Today's Quote
paragraphs: Walk through each sensitivity scenario in Chapter 7 because together they tell a decisive story. At 12.5% to 13.2% normalized ROE instead of 13.8%, Justified P/B compresses to 1.44x–1.55x on $234E book value, yielding $336.96 to $363.17 per share. If 14% below-investment-grade fixed income ($20.04 billion), $17.53 billion in illiquid private equity ($7.08 billion unfunded), and a 10-distribution-day market downtrend lift cost of equity by 100 basis points to 10.75%, fair value drops to $332.44.

Finally, if half of today's $24.79-per-share AOCI deficit persists alongside a 1.46x multiple de-rating, fair value falls to $323.54. Notice that all four stressed values—from $300.56 in the Bear Case up to $363.17—sit below today's $371.63 stock price. Paying 1.72x ex-AOCI book (1.94x reported) leaves zero margin of safety.
